newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: EU sees start of membership talks in early 1998.
newsitem.headline: EU sees start of membership talks in early 1998.

text.p: Negotiations with potential new members of the European Union will most probably start at the beginning of 1998, president of the European Commission Jacques Santer said on Friday.
"The current moment is very important as negotiations (with potential members) will probably start in the beginning of 1998," Santer told a news conference during his first visit to Ljubljana.
A precondition for Slovenia to be in the first group of countries to start negotiations with the EU was the ratification of the association agreement with the EU, signed in June, Santer said.
Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said the ratification would take place no later than May.

"One of the main agreements reached in the new coalition was that we will continue to approach the EU. The association agreement should be ratified no later than at the May session of parliament," Drnovsek said.

In February, over three months after a general election, Drnovsek of the centre-left Liberal Democrats formed a new government in coalition with the conservative People's Party and pensioners' party Desus.
The People's Party said earlier it supported Slovenia's membership in the EU but said Slovenia should first ensure protection of national interests, mainly agriculture.

"Although a small country, Slovenia should not be afraid that it would lose its own identity by joining the EU. Membership in the EU can increase the country's national and cultural identity and its political power," Santer said.
Apart from Slovenia, Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovakia, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Romania and Bulgaria have all applied for EU membership.
